prompt:
Write 9 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1085; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment kept growing well beyond what this injury usually needs, with more visits and new services added month after month.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened for a side impact collision at an intersection. Claimant reports neck and back strain and is represented by counsel. Driver is named on the policy.

Entry 2: Police report confirms the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of the collision. Scene photos show damage consistent with the described impact.

Entry 3: Vehicle damage pattern matches the reported side impact. No prior damage to the vehicle is known, and nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the coverage start.

Entry 4: Claimant's initial recorded statement describes the collision consistently with the police report. No independent witnesses have come forward to add to the account.

Entry 5: Reported neck and back strain is consistent with the type and force of the crash. No prior injury to the same body areas appears in available records.

Entry 6: Claimant's account has remained the same in each subsequent conversation, including the call with counsel present.

Entry 7: Medical treatment began promptly after the collision. Visit frequency has risen steadily, and new services have been added each month, well beyond what this injury typically requires.

Entry 8: Referred the treatment escalation to the medical review unit for an independent records assessment. Counsel has been informed that the file is under review.

Entry 9: File remains open pending the medical review outcome and receipt of outstanding treatment records. Next follow-up set for the review team's response.
